extracted.intended_audience: U.S. importers of fish and fish products, customs brokers, foreign exporting-nation officials, and trade-community stakeholders interacting with NMFS/CBP on seafood import compliance
extracted.subtask_short: certification of admissibility for seafood imports
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and procedures for using a Certification of Admissibility (COA) to permit entry of seafood otherwise subject to import prohibitions, including required permits, data fields, electronic ACE filing, recordkeeping, and prohibitions. Applies to COA use under the MMPA, Moratorium Protection Act, and ATCA.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Fisheries Trade Permit (IFTP) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who imports fish or fish products for which a COA fish harvest record form is required must possess a valid International Fisheries Trade Permit (IFTP) issued under §300.322; only persons residing in the United States are eligible to apply (a resident agent of a nonresident corporation may apply).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NMFS-issued IFTP number for the importer of record must be provided via the ACE portal. See §300.322 and §300.352 for eligibility and filing obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing via ACE at time of entry
rubrics_metrics.description: The importer of record must electronically file, at the time of entry or in advance of entry, the data sets and documentation required under this subpart with U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) via the ACE portal to determine admissibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific instructions on submitting the required data sets and document images are in the ACE Implementation Guide for NMFS incorporated in CATAIR appendix PGA. An ACE entry filing is required for applicable fish or fish products regardless of shipment value.

rubrics_metrics.name: COA completion, certification, and validation
rubrics_metrics.description: The COA fish harvest record form must be properly completed and signed by a duly authorized official of the exporting nation; it must also be validated and signed by the importer of record and submitted to NMFS in a format specified by NMFS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within 24 hours of release of the product by CBP the importer must submit a copy of the COA (or other approved documentation) via the Document Image System (DIS) for ACE. Nations subject to import prohibitions may use their own form or aggregate catch documentation if NMFS finds it satisfies all requirements of this subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: COA required data elements
rubrics_metrics.description: The COA (or approved form) must include specified data: species (ASFIS 3-alpha code), product form(s) at first landing, quantity and/or weight (aggregate allowed), location(s) of first landing/transshipment/delivery, date(s) of first landing/transshipment/delivery, name of entity(ies) to which fish was landed/delivered, and 10-digit HTSUS codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional required data: (for wild harvest) gear type(s), capture area(s), flag state of harvesting vessel(s), and vessel information (name, authorization, unique vessel identifier) which may be omitted in aggregate reporting; (for aquaculture) farm/facility name(s) and location; also include NMFS-issued IFTP number and U.S. customs entry number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information accuracy and exact match requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Information entered into the ACE portal must be complete and accurate and must match exactly the information provided on the COA fish harvest record form or other approved documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If COA data entered in ACE show admissibility criteria are met, the entry will be processed and shipment released; if COA data are missing, invalid, or indicate inadmissibility, the entry will be rejected. Importers filing under incorrect HTSUS or misrepresenting shipments may be subject to penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability regardless of value and CBP exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: All products subject to subpart S are subject to the subpart's requirements regardless of value and notwithstanding any CBP exemptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An ACE entry filing is required for applicable fish or fish products regardless of shipment value; CBP exemptions do not relieve COA obligations under this subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping and inspection availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Importers of record must retain records of the information reported at entry under this subpart in electronic or paper format and make them available for inspection at the importer's place of business or submit them to NMFS upon request for a period of 2 years from the date of import.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Import shipments and supporting information may be selected for inspection on a pre- or post-release basis to verify entry information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibitions and unlawful acts
rubrics_metrics.description: It is unlawful for any person subject to U.S. jurisdiction to violate any provision of this subpart or the conditions of any IFTP, or to import fish or fish products subject to restrictions and documentation requirements without a valid IFTP or without submitting complete and accurate information and documentation required under this subpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These prohibitions are in addition to prohibitions under other applicable regulations (e.g., 50 CFR 216.12(d), 300.4, 300.325, 635.71). Violations can lead to denial of entry and penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate reporting flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: For aggregate harvests involving multiple small-scale vessels, the importer may provide total quantity and/or weight as landed/delivered and may omit certain vessel information (vessel name, authorization, vessel number) for aggregate reporting; exporting nations may provide aggregated catch documentation in lieu of the COA form if it satisfies this subpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NMFS will consider grouping/aggregate approaches but seeks comment on vessel identifiers and grouping to balance enforcement and burden. NMFS may accept foreign nation catch certificates if they meet the certification requirements relative to the trade restriction.

rubrics_metrics.name: HTSUS coding and country-of-origin determination
rubrics_metrics.description: U.S. importers must specify 10-digit codes based on the U.S. Harmonized Tariff Schedule (HTSUS); an entry matching a specified combination of HTSUS code and country of origin will trigger the COA data requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Importers should work with foreign exporters to determine the applicable HTSUS code; filing under an incorrect HTSUS code or intentionally misrepresenting shipment information may result in penalties. See hts.usitc.gov for HTSUS details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation and functional equivalence of foreign certification systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Nations subject to import prohibitions may use their own form or electronic catch documentation systems in lieu of NMFS' COA form if NMFS finds the provided information satisfies all requirements of this subpart and is the functional equivalent of NMFS' COA fish harvest record form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NMFS will work with exporting nations to determine application, may consider publishing lists of duly authorized officials where helpful, and will coordinate approaches to avoid disruption to legitimate trade; however, NMFS is not mandating government-to-government electronic transfers in this rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importer validation prior to DIS upload
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to submission via the Document Image System, the importer of record must validate that the contents of the shipment were accurately described on the COA and that all relevant parties (including the importer) have signed the form as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The validated copy must be submitted with the U.S. customs entry number noted via DIS within 24 hours of release by CBP; failure to validate may result in rejection or enforcement action.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACE automation, message set, and software integration
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP will develop functionality in ACE to allow NMFS to specify trade restrictions and to accept the prescribed message set for COA data; importers and customs brokers should coordinate with software developers to generate required ACE message sets and avoid repetitive data entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific instructions are in the ACE Implementation Guide for NMFS (CATAIR appendix PGA). NMFS and CBP will test automation in ACE certification environment and provide time for testing; NMFS will not fully digitalize COA certification for all trading partners in this rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal applicability of COA relative to trade restriction effective date
rubrics_metrics.description: COA requirements apply upon the effective date of a trade restriction; however, importers may be allowed entry if they report a harvest date prior to the effective date of the trade restriction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Importers must report harvest date on the COA and in ACE to demonstrate that product was harvested before the effective date of the restriction to qualify for admissibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation and cross-reference across statutory programs
rubrics_metrics.description: The COA requirements are consolidated into 50 CFR part 300, subpart S and apply across COA-related provisions under the MMPA, the Moratorium Protection Act, and ATCA; applicable CFR provisions are cross-referenced to subpart S for COA procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory changes update references in 50 CFR 216.24(h), 300.207, and 635.40 to rely on subpart S for COA procedures and definitions; the COA is the attestation that products are not subject to import prohibitions under specified CFR sections.
